text.headline: Platinum Slumps as Industrial Metals Retreat
text.tone: A firmer dollar and weaker demand prospects added to pressure on platinum, which fell more sharply than silver and copper.
lead: Platinum fell 4.9%, the most significant move of the session on the [[metals|Hard Assets Terminal]]. In contrast, VIX volatility index rose 18.7%, a sign that investors did not move in a single direction. Gold moved the same way, which gives the move more weight.

A likely reading: platinum and copper fell together, a sign of softer expectations for industrial and car-making demand. Silver fell with copper: more than half of silver demand is industrial, so it trades partly like a factory metal.
Across asset classes, US 10-year yield fell 3 bp and EUR/USD fell 0.2%. A firmer dollar weighed on gold, which becomes dearer for buyers paying in other currencies.

What to watch: whether the main move holds over the next sessions or fades, and whether other markets begin to follow. A broader shift would confirm today's reading; a quick reversal would point to a short-lived adjustment. The [[outlook|Market Outlook]] places it in the longer trend.

briefs.markets: US 10-year yield fell 3 bp to 5.12% (latest data: Nov 16), leaving the gap over the 2-year at +29 bp. The [[markets|Financial Markets]] page has yields, commodities and currencies.
briefs.energy: Brent crude rose 2.2% to $92.14 (latest data: Nov 11); US natural gas (Henry Hub) rose 3.8% to $3.00 (latest data: Nov 10). Benchmarks, power prices and supply data on the [[energy|Energy Terminal]].
briefs.crypto: Bitcoin fell 1.2% to $64,031; EUR/USD fell 0.2% to 1.0989. Live rates and a converter on [[crypto|Crypto & Currencies]].
briefs.metals: Gold fell 2.9% to $3,751; Copper fell 1.1% to $13,226/t. Precious and base metals on the [[metals|Hard Assets Terminal]].
briefs.estate: House prices are rising in 61 of the 69 countries we track over the past year; Moldova leads at +33.7%. Country data on the [[estate|Estate Index]].
briefs.corporate: This week's top-ranked bank is East West Bank and the top company is APA Corporation, under a risk-on backdrop. Rankings on the [[corporate|Corporate Monitor]].
briefs.outlook: Our quarterly outlook reads the backdrop as risk-off; Cybersecurity leads the five themes we follow. Full rankings on the [[outlook|Market Outlook]].
briefs.islamic: EB Shariah US 100 fell 0.7% to 116.90 (latest data: Nov 13); it is +14.1% this year against +12.2% for the unscreened market. Screens and funds on [[islamic|Islamic Investment]].
